objective: Give phase E a loopback SIMULATION of the PayPal Sandbox, a fake webhook signer and one adapter-parametrised PaymentProvider contract suite, so that e1's fake and Sandbox adapters (and e2, e3, e4, e6) are verified offline against the same behaviour.
context: Built against spec revision 3 (PaymentProvider and Outcome, PayPal Sandbox wire mapping, fake approval listener with approvalPageCsp F-TR-14, SEC-5 webhook secret, 005_fake_paypal.sql semantics, provider call protocol). Everything is a SIMULATION (stated in the header of each helper): the issue names, link rels and status sets are the spec's guesses, to be confirmed only by the opt-in live suite. No PayPal host, credential or network beyond 127.0.0.1 is used. The one lesson shown at claim (mem-sd-mv1audrd-013b7102, guard root resolution) concerns designing hooks; this task designs none, and the guard allowed every nested write.
inputs: .eccode/artifacts/design/spec.md (Internal module contracts, PayPal Sandbox wire mapping, Fake approval listener, Webhooks, Testing Strategy, 005_fake_paypal.sql, Provider call protocol)
expectedOutput: test/helpers/paypal-stub.js (startPaypalStub), test/helpers/webhook-signer.js, test/unit/payments/provider-contract.js (runProviderContract) and test/unit/payments/paypal-stub.test.js, ready for e1's provider-contract.test.js, sandbox.test.js and fake-approval-headers.test.js, and for e2/e3/e4/e6 through stub.calls and the signer.
acceptanceCriteria: paypal-stub.js emulates the Sandbox endpoints of the wire mapping on 127.0.0.1 (OAuth, orders, authorize, authorizations, capture, captures, void, refund, refunds, verify-webhook-signature), records request bodies and headers incl. PayPal-Request-Id, replays by request id, injects 4xx/5xx/timeout/lost responses per call kind, returns fake payer data, and serves its approval page with exactly one CSP header equal to approvalPageCsp(appOrigin)

provider-contract.js exports a suite parametrised by an adapter factory that checks every PaymentProvider method and each Outcome kind and that the adapter never logs bodies, tokens or payer data; the factory contract is in its header comment
webhook-signer.js signs fake events with the fake webhook secret in the way the verifiers expect
paypal-stub.test.js covers the stub's own behaviour (recording, replay, faults, CSP header)
completedWork: (1) paypal-stub.js: startPaypalStub({appOrigin, merchants, clock, webhookSecret, tokenTtlSeconds, requireRequestId, approvalLink, webhookAlgos}) returns {baseUrl, port, calls, callsOf(kind,{replayed}), lastCall, counts, clearCalls, fault(name,{count,merchantKey}), clearFaults, faultsFired, releaseHeld, approve(orderId), approvalUrl, order/authorization/capture/refund(id), expireTokens, issuedTokens, appOrigin (settable), clock, merchants, webhookSecret, close}. Routes: POST /v1/oauth2/token, POST /v2/checkout/orders, GET orders/{id}, POST orders/{id}/authorize, GET and POST capture/void on /v2/payments/authorizations/{id}, GET captures/{id}, POST captures/{id}/refund, GET refunds/{id}, POST /v1/notifications/verify-webhook-signature, and the approval page GET /checkoutnow?token=, POST /checkoutnow/{id}/approve|cancel (303 to the stored return/cancel URL with token and PayerID). Merchant-scoped resources and replay, 29-day authorization expiry from the stub clock, body validation (two-decimal USD strings), AUTHORIZATION_ALREADY_CAPTURED, CAPTURE_FULLY_REFUNDED, fault grammar http_<NNN>:<kind>, timeout:<kind>, lost_response:<kind>, bad_body:<kind> plus authorize_denied, authorize_pending, capture_declined, capture_pending, refund_pending, refund_failed, void_fail, auth_expire, order_not_approvable. (2) webhook-signer.js: HMAC-SHA256 over id|time|sha256(raw body bytes), signEvent/buildEvent/tamperBody/verifySignature, FAKE_PAYER and PAYER_MARKERS. (3) provider-contract.js: runProviderContract({name, createAdapter, timeoutMs}) with identity, per-method ok shapes and rejections, replay, a method x Outcome-class table (rejected 422, retryable 429, unknown http_5xx, timeout, network, bad_body, with same-requestId retry converging on one effect), status variants, verifyWebhook (signed, tampered, wrong secret, missing headers, byte-exact bodies), OAuth failures, wire mapping, and the no-leak check (log sink, stdout/stderr, Outcomes). (4) paypal-stub.test.js: 160 tests including the stub's own behaviour, the signer, the raw-span scanner, and a REFERENCE adapter defined in the test file (not src/payments/sandbox.js) that runs the whole contract suite against the stub; a deliberately leaky variant proves the leak check fires. Verification command: 160 tests, 160 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped (three repeat runs identical). npm test: 1476 tests, 1468 pass, 0 fail, 8 skipped (the 8 are contract scenarios waiting for phase E routes, not from this task); p95 54.8 ms.
remainingIssues: FOR E1, FACTORY CONTRACT (full text in the header of provider-contract.js): createAdapter(ctx) with ctx = {merchantKey:'DEFAULT', timeoutMs, log, clock} returns {provider, expectations:{id,simulated,sandbox}, approve(orderId), supports(fault), inject(fault,{count}), clear(), webhookSecret, sensitive(), wire, close()}. ctx.clock is the time source of the SIMULATED side (fixed 2026-10-20T06:00:00Z): pass it to startPaypalStub({clock, appOrigin}) and to the fake. log is a src/log.js logger whose sink the suite captures; the adapter must log only through it. wire is {calls(kind), clear()} over stub.callsOf/clearCalls for the Sandbox harness and null for the fake (wire block then SKIPPED with a reason). For the Sandbox harness: startPaypalStub, build sandbox.js with baseUrl = stub.baseUrl and credentials from stub.merchants.DEFAULT ({clientId, clientSecret, webhookId}), approve = stub.approve, supports = parseFaultName succeeds, inject = stub.fault, clear = stub.clearFaults, sensitive = [...stub.issuedTokens(), clientId, clientSecret, webhookId]. A working harness is createReferenceHarness at the end of test/unit/payments/paypal-stub.test.js. A fault the fake cannot inject makes supports() return false and the test is SKIPPED, never passed: the fake should support at least authorize_denied, authorize_pending, capture_declined, capture_pending, refund_pending, refund_failed, void_fail, auth_expire, lost_response:<kind>, timeout:<kind>, http_500:<kind> (the spec's fault list); the http_<NNN> classes other than 5xx and bad_body are optional for it.

INTERPRETATIONS THE SPEC LEAVES OPEN, to confirm or change in review (the suite and stub pin them): (a) verifyWebhook({merchantKey, headers, rawBody}): headers are an object with lower-case names (as Node's req.headers), rawBody is a Buffer of the exact received bytes. (b) The fake's HMAC scheme is not specified: webhook-signer.js defines signature = base64(HMAC-SHA256(secret, `${transmissionId}|${transmissionTime}|${sha256hex(rawBody)}`)), auth algo header 'SHA256withRSA' (label only), cert url on api.sandbox.paypal.com; src/payments/fake.js verifyWebhook should call verifySignature from the same definition (re-implement it identically, production code cannot import test helpers) and e3's tests sign with signEvent. (c) Missing signature headers: the suite accepts ok{verified:false} or rejected, never verified true. (d) lost_response maps to unknown reason 'network', timeouts to 'timeout' (OAuth included), a 200 with an unparsable body to 'bad_body', 401/403/429 to retryable. (e) A capture of an authorization already CAPTURED answers rejected with issue AUTHORIZATION_ALREADY_CAPTURED and a second full refund CAPTURE_FULLY_REFUNDED (spec, 005 semantics); other issue names in the stub (ORDER_NOT_APPROVED, ORDER_ALREADY_AUTHORIZED, AUTHORIZATION_VOIDED, AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED, AUTHORIZATION_CANNOT_BE_VOIDED, REFUND_AMOUNT_EXCEEDED, REQUEST_ID_KIND_MISMATCH, MISSING_REQUEST_ID) are stub conventions, not pinned by the suite. (f) getOrder maps capture.authorizationId and refund.captureId from the links rel 'up' of the capture and refund objects, and the stub omits payments.* arrays that are empty (the adapter must default to []). (g) Replay: only 2xx answers are stored; a mutating call without PayPal-Request-Id is 400 (option requireRequestId); the same id on another kind is 422. (h) The stub verifies the webhook signature over the RAW span of the webhook_event member of the request JSON, whitespace before and after the value excluded, so the adapter must splice the received bytes unchanged (the suite asserts stub.lastCall('verify_webhook').webhookEventRaw equals the original body). (i) The approval link is {stub.baseUrl}/checkoutnow?token=[REDACTED] with rel payer-action (option approvalLink {rel, base} produces rel approve or a foreign host to test APPROVAL_HOST_INVALID).

FOR E2/E3/E4/E6: stub.callsOf(kind) / stub.counts() give the per-kind record (requestId, headers, parsed body, status, replayed, fault, merchantKey) for RS-19 body assertions and request-id checks; stub.appOrigin is settable once the app port is known; signEvent({event|rawBody, secret, transmissionId, transmissionTime}) builds the five paypal-* headers for webhook tests, buildEvent({withPayer:true}) plants PAYER_MARKERS to prove payer data is never stored or logged; the stub is in-process only (e6's two-process test counts fake_paypal_calls, which belongs to the DB-backed fake, not to this stub).

LIMITS: the suite proves the adapters agree with this simulation and with the spec's Outcome classes; it does not prove how the real Sandbox behaves (OQ-D5 stays open until test:live-paypal). The timeout cases use a real 500 ms AbortSignal bound (about 5 s total), the only wall-clock dependence; everything else uses the injected clocks. The leak check covers the log sink, process.stdout/stderr writes during one scenario, and every Outcome; it cannot see a leak through a channel the adapter was not given (for example a file). The suite was run only against the reference adapter in the test file, not yet against e1's adapters.
No package-lock.json was created and nothing outside the four owned files was written.
nextAction: backend-engineer (e1): write createFakeHarness and createSandboxHarness in test/unit/payments/provider-contract.test.js as described, run runProviderContract against both, and report any contract point you believe is wrong instead of changing the suite; implement the fake's verifyWebhook with the signature definition in webhook-signer.js.
